{{Short description|Three-dimensional packing puzzle}}
[[Image:Herzberger Quader.jpg|thumb|upright|The Herzberger Quader, as it was published on the occasion of the 50th anniversary of high school graduation in Herzberg]]

The '''Herzberger Quader''' is a [[Mechanical puzzle#Assembly|solid dissection puzzle]] invented by German mathematics teacher Gerhard Schulze.<ref name="alpha1990">{{cite journal |url=https://mathematikalpha.de/?smd_process_download=1&download_id=9292#19 |journal=Mathematische Schülerzeitschrift alpha |language=de |volume=24 |year=1990 |issue=6 |page=137 |author=B. Junghanns |title=31. Ausstellung 'Herzberger Spiele'}}</ref>
It was named after his home-town [[Herzberg (Elster)|Herzberg]], and Quader is the latin-derived German word for a [[rectangular cuboid]].

== Design ==
[[File:herzberger_quader_cuboid.svg|thumb|upright|The Herzberger Quader pieces packed into a 2&nbsp;×&nbsp;4&nbsp;×&nbsp;5 cuboid]]
The Herzberger Quader consists of a set of all possible [[polycube]]s from dicube to tetracubes.<ref name="alpha1997">{{cite journal |journal=Alpha – Mathematik Als Hobby |language=de |volume=31 |year=1997 |pages=73–105 |author=Gerhard Schulze |title=Der Herzberger Quader}}</ref>
The eleven pieces together have 40 unit cubes and thus can be stored in a 2 × 4 × 5 box.<ref name="alpha1997" />

== Possible problems ==
{{float right clear none|[[File:Soma_cube_figures.svg|thumb|Some Soma cube figures assembled from the non-cuboidal Herzberger Quader pieces]]}}
Besides stowing the Herzberger Quader in its box there are a lot of figures that can be built using all parts. Various subsets can be used to form a 3 × 3 × 3 cube, one of them is the famous [[Soma cube]].<ref name="alpha1997" />

Much more demanding tasks ask for the number of all different possibilities to arrange the initial parts in a certain figure. Or proofs are to be given for which figures can be realized or not realized with which polycubes.<ref name="alpha1997" />

== History ==

Author of the Herzberger Quader is [[Oberstudienrat]] Gerhard Schulze (1919–1995), who was intensively engaged in [[recreational mathematics|mathematical games]] during his extracurricular activities in the years 1982–1994.<ref name="alpha1994">{{cite journal |journal=Alpha – Mathematik Als Hobby |language=de |volume=28 |year=1994 |issue=1 |pages=16–17 |author=Gerhard Schulze |title=10 Jahre 'Herzberger Spiele'}}</ref>
On the occasion of the 800th anniversary of his hometown Herzberg in 1984, the Herzberger Quader was produced for the first time and thus made known to a broad public.
Today, the Herzberger Quader is suggested to be used in the context of [[mathematics education]].<ref name="fachmoderator">{{cite web |url=http://www.fachmoderator-mathematik.de/index.php?id=125 |website=Fachmoderator Mathematik |language=de |author=Dirk Tönnies |access-date=2023-12-05 |title=Herzberger Quader}}</ref><ref name="meinunterricht">{{cite web |url=https://app.meinunterricht.de/dokument/5cdac28a812e3c0015c4f556 |website=meinUnterricht |language=de |author=Andreas Koepsell |access-date=2023-12-05 |title=Bauen mit Klötzen}}</ref>
